span.p:
record 3821 — the only plaintext one.
Position-independent x86-64 that walks the
PEB and resolves exports by a 64-bit hash

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
record 9990 — 118 packed bytes,
i.e. 40 bytes of ciphertext

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
the program you can actually run:
four hard-coded 'magic' sums, each answering
with an XOR'd taunt. All four are decoys.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
DataDirectory[4], the certificate table:
529,568 bytes, about 100x a real signature.
It lives outside every section, so the Windows
loader never maps it into memory.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
chain: FLARE-ON Root CA ->
'Never Gonna Let You Down' ->
'Never Gonna Give You Up'

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
leaf extension under private OID
1.3.6.1.4.1.1337.1, 526 KB:
a SEQUENCE of 1035 records, each
SEQUENCE { INTEGER id, OCTET STRING data }

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
the loader opens its own module, seeks to
DataDirectory[4], reads the certificate blob,
and walks that same DER structure by record id

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
per record: key = MD5(master_key || id),
folded to a 32-bit seed by h = h*31 + byte

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
layer 1 — XOR with the low byte of
state = state * 1103515245 + 12345

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
layer 2 — a second LCG, seeded from the master
key alone, drives the unpack loop: copy one byte,
then skip (r mod 3) + 1 junk bytes

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
VirtualAlloc RWX, call with three arguments,
zero the page, VirtualFree.
Exactly one function exists at a time.
